newsitem.title: CZECH REPUBLIC: AssiDoman seeks last Czech Sepap shares.
newsitem.headline: AssiDoman seeks last Czech Sepap shares.

text.p: The Swedish pulp and paper group AssiDoman AB made a public offer on Friday to buy remaining common stock in its already majority-owned Czech unit, Sepap a.s., at 1,250 crowns per share.

In a statement published in the Czech daily newspaper Lidove Noviny, AssiDoman said its public offer for the shares was valid from July 29 through September 29 of this year, and could be transacted through either of the two Czech bourses.

According to Czech law, a shareholder acquiring more than 50 percent of a any issue, must offer to buy remaining stock from other shareholders at a price equal to the average price quoted on the Prague bourse over the past six months.

"The reason for this public offer...is, beside its legal obligation, an attempt by the offerer to attain 100 percent ownership of the company in order to cancel public tradibility in shares of the company (Sepap)," the statement said.
Sepap shares were fixed on the Prague Stock Exchange on Friday at 1,264 crowns, down 11 from Thursday's close.
AssiDoman has acquired a 90 percent stake in Sepap, the largest Czech paper producer, after buying a 51 percent stake in May from the Cyprus-based investment firm Daventree.
The Swedish company said it paid about $130 million, for the Daventree shares putting the purchase price at well over 2,000 crowns per share.
The remaining shares are believed to be held mostly by individuals and investment funds.
The public offer was arranged by the Czech subsidiary of Citibank and Citicorp Securities.
